observation.visible_scene: A woman with her hair in a bun, wearing a white long-sleeve top with an open back, black flared pants and a face mask, stands in a mirrored dance studio facing the wall of mirrors. A ballet barre and a small phone on the floor are visible; her reflection occupies the right portion of the frame. The camera framing and background remain fixed throughout.
visible_changes: At the start her arms are already raised overhead with hands close together forming a rounded circle, a pose she holds with only minor adjustments through the early frames.
Her arms then open outward and upward from the overhead circle into a wide raised 'V' position.
The arms gradually lower from the wide 'V' down toward the sides, ending bent and low near her hips.
As the arms settle low, one leg extends out to the side/back with the foot pointed, the torso turning slightly.
The extended leg is held in that side/back position, with small shifts in angle, through the final frame; the clip ends with the leg still extended.
Her reflection reproduces each of these arm and leg positions simultaneously (mirror image, not a second person).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the overhead arm circle was reached from a lower position before the clip began.
What follows after the leg extension (whether the leg returns or transitions to another step).
Any music, cues, or instruction driving the movement.
uncertain_details: The exact ballet terminology (port de bras, tendu/dégagé) is inferred from posture only.
The degree of torso rotation is subtle and partly obscured by the arm positions.
Camera motion is judged static because the mirror seams, door and barre stay in fixed image positions.
